name: Valletta
meta: Book direct holiday apartments and traditional homes in Valletta, Malta's capital. Professionally managed, licensed stays with a local team available 24/7.
intro: Valletta is a UNESCO World Heritage city built by the Knights of St John in the 1500s, and the whole capital fits inside its bastion walls. Staying here means stepping out of your door onto limestone streets, baroque churches and harbour views, with cafés, museums and the Sliema and Three Cities ferries all within a ten-minute walk.
why: Everything on foot: St John's Co-Cathedral, the Upper Barrakka Gardens and the waterfront are minutes away
Ferries to Sliema and the Three Cities leave from the city
The main bus terminus connects you to every corner of Malta
Evenings in the capital: wine bars, restaurants and summer festivals in the streets
tips: Valletta homes are historic buildings. Expect stairs, character and softer light in some rooms.
Cars are not practical inside the walls. Arrive by taxi, bus or ferry and walk.
Book early for spring and autumn, which are the busiest seasons in the capital.
faq: Is Valletta a good base for exploring Malta?
Yes. The main bus terminus is at the city gate, the ferries to Sliema and the Three Cities leave from the harbour, and most of the island is within 45 minutes by bus.
Are the Valletta homes licensed?
Yes. Every property we manage holds a Malta Tourism Authority holiday licence and displays its licence number.

name: Sliema
h1: Holiday apartments and rooms in Sliema, Malta
meta: Book direct seafront apartments, a design townhouse with splash pool and private rooms in Sliema, Malta. Managed locally, best price guaranteed on direct bookings.
intro: Sliema is Malta's seafront town: a long promenade, rocky beaches you swim from, shopping at Tigné Point and a ferry that reaches Valletta in ten minutes. It is the most convenient base on the island if you want the sea, restaurants and transport all at the door.
why: Swim from the rocks along the promenade or at Exiles beach
Ferry to Valletta in 10 minutes, buses to everywhere else
Hundreds of cafés, restaurants and shops within walking distance
Walk to St Julian's and Spinola Bay along the seafront
tips: Seafront flats are in demand in summer. Book direct early for the best rate.
The promenade is flat and well lit, ideal for evening walks and morning runs.
Supermarkets, pharmacies and bus stops are never more than a few minutes away.
faq: Can I swim in Sliema?
Yes. The Sliema coastline is rocky rather than sandy, with ladders and flat rock platforms along the promenade. Exiles and Fond Għadir are the most popular spots.
How far is Sliema from the airport?
About 25 to 30 minutes by taxi. We can arrange an airport transfer on request.

name: St Julian's
h1: Holiday homes and apartments in St Julian's, Malta
meta: Book direct houses and apartments in St Julian's, Malta: Spinola Bay, Balluta Bay and Paceville. Terraces, BBQs and professionally managed stays.
intro: St Julian's wraps around three bays, Balluta, Spinola and St George's, and is where Malta goes out to eat. Fishing boats in Spinola Bay, restaurants along the water, a sandy beach at St George's Bay and Paceville's nightlife a few streets away. Our homes here sit in the quieter residential streets just behind the bays.
why: Spinola Bay restaurants and the seafront promenade on foot
St George's Bay sandy beach and beach clubs
Paceville nightlife close by, quiet streets to sleep in
Direct buses to Valletta, Sliema and the north
tips: Our St Julian's houses have private terraces with BBQs, ideal for groups.
Paceville is lively at night. Our homes are a few streets away, in residential blocks.
San Gwann, just inland, is a quiet alternative a short walk from Balluta Bay.
faq: Is St Julian's noisy at night?
Paceville is the nightlife district and gets loud at weekends. Our properties are in residential streets around Spinola and Balluta Bay, away from the clubs, and all have quiet hours.
Which beach is closest?
St George's Bay is the sandy beach in St Julian's. Balluta Bay has a small sandy cove and the Sliema rocks are a short walk away.

name: The Three Cities
h1: Guest houses and rooms in the Three Cities, Malta
meta: Book direct private ensuite rooms in Cospicua and Senglea, the Three Cities of Malta. Family-run guest house and a renovated palazzo, minutes from Valletta by ferry.
intro: Cospicua (Bormla), Senglea (Isla) and Birgu (Vittoriosa) face Valletta across the Grand Harbour. They are older than the capital, far quieter, and still lived in by locals. A ferry crosses to Valletta in minutes, the waterfront at Dock 1 and the Birgu marina are lined with restaurants, and the Gardjola Gardens in Senglea have one of the best views in Malta.
why: Ferry to Valletta in minutes, or a 10-minute bus
The most authentic, local side of the harbour
Waterfront restaurants at Dock 1 and the Birgu marina
Close to the American University of Malta
tips: Our rooms here are in two guest houses: a family-run house in Cospicua and Jungle Palazzo, a renovated old palazzo in Senglea.
Every room has a private bathroom. Kitchens and rooftop terraces are shared.
Ideal for couples and solo travellers who want character at a sensible price.
faq: Are the Three Cities well connected?
Yes. The Cospicua ferry crosses to Valletta in about 10 minutes, and buses run to Valletta, the airport and the south of the island.
Do the rooms have private bathrooms?
Yes. Every room we offer in Cospicua and Senglea has its own private bathroom, with AC and heating included.

name: Msida, Pietà and Ta' Xbiex
h1: Apartments and penthouses in Msida, Pietà and Ta' Xbiex, Malta
meta: Book direct penthouses with pools and terraces, and modern apartments in Msida, Pietà and Ta' Xbiex, five minutes from Valletta. Managed locally.
intro: Msida, Pietà and Ta' Xbiex sit around Marsamxett Harbour between Valletta and Sliema. This is the central hub of Malta: five minutes to the capital, ten to Sliema and St Julian's, with the yacht marinas, the University of Malta and Mater Dei Hospital all here. Our homes in this area are the ones with the big terraces, private pools and designer interiors.
why: Five minutes to Valletta, ten to Sliema and St Julian's
Marinas, waterfront walks and local restaurants
Penthouses with private pools and large terraces
Quiet residential streets, easy parking
tips: Pick this area for space: terraces, backyards and pools are far easier to find here than in Valletta or Sliema.
Ta' Xbiex is the quiet, leafy corner by the yacht marina.
Buses to every part of the island pass through Msida.
faq: Is Msida close to the beach?
The nearest swimming is the Sliema and Gzira seafront, about 10 minutes away. Sandy beaches in the north are 30 to 40 minutes by bus or car.
Why stay here instead of Valletta?
More space for the same budget: terraces, pools and parking, with the capital still five minutes away.

name: St Paul's Bay
h1: Holiday apartments in St Paul's Bay and Bugibba, Malta
meta: Book direct sea-view apartments in St Paul's Bay, Malta. Close to Bugibba, boat trips to Comino and the Blue Lagoon, and the sandy beaches of the north.
intro: St Paul's Bay and Bugibba are the holiday heart of the north coast: a long seafront promenade, boat trips to Comino and the Blue Lagoon from the harbour, and the sandy beaches of Mellieħa and Golden Bay a short drive away. A relaxed, sunny base for families and anyone who wants the sea first and the cities second.
why: Boat trips to Comino and the Blue Lagoon from the bay
Mellieħa Bay and Golden Bay sandy beaches nearby
Seafront promenade with restaurants and cafés
Easy ferry to Gozo from Ċirkewwa
tips: Our penthouse here has a sea-view terrace with BBQ and electric shades for the afternoon sun.
Buses to Valletta take about 45 minutes. A hire car makes the north easy.
Summer is peak season on the north coast. Book early.
faq: How do I get to the Blue Lagoon from St Paul's Bay?
Boat trips to Comino leave from the harbour in Bugibba most days from spring to autumn, and from Ċirkewwa all year.
Is St Paul's Bay good for families?
Yes. The promenade is flat, there are playgrounds and a water park nearby, and the sandy beaches of the north are a short drive away.

name: Marsaskala
short: A quiet seaside town in the south east
meta: Book direct a modern two-bedroom apartment near the sea in Marsaskala, Malta. Quiet seaside town 20 minutes from the airport, close to St Thomas Bay.
intro: Marsaskala is a working seaside town in the south east of Malta, where locals swim, fish and eat out along the bay. It is twenty minutes from the airport, close to St Thomas Bay and the St Peter's Pool swimming spot, and a calm alternative to the busier resorts on the other side of the island.
why: Quiet seafront town with local restaurants
St Thomas Bay and St Peter's Pool for swimming
20 minutes from the airport
Close to Marsaxlokk fishing village and its Sunday market
tips: Our apartment here is brand new, with a large front terrace and a lift.
Marsaxlokk, with its coloured boats and fish restaurants, is 10 minutes away.
A car helps if you plan day trips to the north of the island.
faq: Is Marsaskala far from Valletta?
About 25 minutes by car or 35 by bus.
Where can I swim in Marsaskala?
St Thomas Bay has a sandy beach, and St Peter's Pool, a natural rock pool, is a short drive away.

name: Rabat and Mdina
short: The silent city and the west
h1: Townhouse with pool near Mdina, Rabat, Malta
meta: Book direct a brand-new townhouse with a rooftop pool in Rabat, steps from Mdina. The best base for Dingli Cliffs, Golden Bay and the west of Malta.
intro: Mdina is Malta's silent city, a walled medieval town on a hill in the centre of the island, and Rabat is the lively town at its gates with the catacombs, bakeries and some of the best restaurants in Malta. From here the Dingli Cliffs, the beaches of Golden Bay and Għajn Tuffieħa, and the whole west of the island are minutes away.
why: Steps from Mdina and its views over the whole island
St Paul's Catacombs and Rabat's traditional bakeries
Dingli Cliffs and the west coast beaches nearby
Cooler evenings and a slower pace than the coast
tips: Our townhouse here has a private rooftop pool overlooking the Mdina skyline.
Mdina at night, after the day visitors leave, is unforgettable.
A hire car is useful in this part of the island.
faq: Can I visit Mdina on foot from Rabat?
Yes. Mdina's main gate is a few minutes' walk from the centre of Rabat.
How far are the beaches?
Golden Bay and Għajn Tuffieħa are about 15 minutes by car.
